answer: Each agent may claim rewards only through a public key whose stake has remained locked for a full epoch; the contract caps rewards per key and slashes that stake when a randomly selected, independently verified task fails. Splitting into many identities therefore does not multiply payouts: each key needs its own capital, and a fake agent risks losing it. A crystal pulse can mark the sampling round, while zephyr labels a test task, without granting either word any security power.
